questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes osteoporosis screening from post-fracture evaluation?
choices: They are identical
Screening applies to people without known osteoporosis or fragility fracture, while a low-trauma fracture requires diagnostic and prevention assessment
DXA is never useful after fracture
Only men need fracture evaluation
questions.explanation: Preventive screening guidance applies to asymptomatic people without known disease or fragility fracture. A low-trauma fracture changes the problem to diagnostic evaluation and secondary fracture prevention.

questions.question: A patient has a T-score in the osteopenia range but a prior vertebral fragility fracture and chronic glucocorticoid exposure. What is the best interpretation?
choices: Fracture risk is necessarily low
Risk can be high despite the T-score and requires contextual treatment planning
The DXA excludes osteoporosis-related care
Only exercise is appropriate
questions.explanation: Absolute fracture risk reflects age, prior fracture, medication exposure, falls, and other factors as well as DXA. A non-osteoporotic T-score does not guarantee low risk.

questions.question: What does a DXA T-score primarily compare?
choices: Bone density with a young-adult reference population
Bone density with only the patient's siblings
Fall risk with vision score
Pain intensity with x-ray severity
questions.explanation: A T-score compares bone mineral density with a young-adult reference population in the appropriate clinical context. It is only one part of fracture-risk assessment.

questions.question: Which history most increases concern for a vertebral compression fracture?
choices: Sudden focal mid-back pain after lifting a light object in an older adult with osteoporosis
Mild soreness after an intense workout in a healthy young adult
Seasonal nasal congestion
A painless normal gait
questions.explanation: Acute focal spinal pain after low-energy stress in a high-risk patient can be a compression fracture and needs targeted evaluation.

questions.question: Why is fall prevention part of osteoporosis treatment?
choices: Fractures happen only from medication adverse effects
Many fractures occur when fragile bone meets a fall, so gait, balance, vision, medication, and home safety matter
Fall prevention replaces bone assessment
Falls are unrelated to hip fracture
questions.explanation: Bone strength and fall risk interact. Effective prevention addresses both pathways through medication review, balance, vision, home safety, and rehabilitation.

questions.question: Which medication review is especially important in fracture-risk assessment?
choices: Systemic glucocorticoids, sedatives, medications causing orthostasis, and agents that affect bone
Only short-term topical moisturizer
Only vaccines
None; medications do not affect fractures
questions.explanation: Medications can increase bone loss or falls. A comprehensive review is essential to prevention and safe therapy selection.

questions.question: A patient with osteoporosis falls and cannot bear weight because of hip pain. What is the best next action?
choices: Wait for routine DXA
Urgent or emergency evaluation for possible hip or pelvic fracture
Start a new resistance program immediately
Assume it is a bruise
questions.explanation: Inability to bear weight after a fall with hip or pelvic pain requires urgent evaluation for fracture. Do not delay for outpatient screening tests.

questions.question: Why should osteoporosis medications not be stopped casually or treated as interchangeable?
choices: All agents have identical risks
Different therapies have distinct renal, calcium, administration, discontinuation, and sequencing considerations
They never need monitoring
Stopping medication always improves bone density
questions.explanation: Therapies differ substantially. Some require specific monitoring or transitions, and stopping certain agents without a plan can be unsafe.

questions.question: What does a low Z-score in a younger adult most appropriately prompt?
choices: Automatic diagnosis of primary osteoporosis only
Consideration of secondary contributors in clinical context
No further assessment
A conclusion that falls are impossible
questions.explanation: A Z-score compares with age-matched peers and can suggest that secondary causes warrant evaluation, interpreted with history and examination.

questions.question: Which FNP action best demonstrates closed-loop fracture prevention after a low-trauma wrist fracture?
choices: Treat the wrist and remove the problem from the chart
Review fracture mechanism, obtain records, assess bone and fall risk, coordinate testing or treatment, and establish follow-up
Order repeated x-rays every week without assessment
Tell the patient fractures are inevitable
questions.explanation: A fragility fracture is an opportunity to prevent the next fracture. Closed-loop care addresses bone risk, falls, medications, rehabilitation, and follow-up.
